source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 146: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions: freeze the model revision, tokenizer, prompt and output distributions, context-length strata, decoding settings, serving engine/version, hardware, runtime, quantization algorithm, bit-width, group size and scales, calibration split, batch/concurrency policy, and cost horizon. Compare the unquantized reference with the weight-only candidate using the same weights before quantization, prompts, seeds, stopping rules, request trace, SLOs, and replica policy; report measured facts with units and distinguish nominal weight storage from total runtime memory.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 146: at fixed quality and tail-latency gates, the quantized candidate lowers cost per accepted output token because reduced resident weight memory improves feasible packing or throughput without introducing material quality, correctness, kernel-support, or failure regressions. Falsify it if any required quality/correctness or p99/error/OOM gate fails, if the engine uses an unreported fallback path, or if a paired cost comparison does not exceed a prespecified minimum benefit. Treat effects as workload-stratum dependent rather than claiming a single average.

Experiment: freeze and checksum both artifacts and run a held-out quality/correctness suite covering each task, long and short contexts, rare tokens, structured outputs, safety/error cases, and representative decoding. Keep calibration data disjoint from evaluation. Use identical warmup, randomized run order, hardware pool, software manifest, and seeded request trace; repeat trials at prespecified offered loads and concurrency levels until uncertainty is adequate. Measure task-level quality, pass/malformed-output/refusal rates, TTFT and TPOT in milliseconds, p50/p95/p99 latency, queueing, requests/s and accepted output tokens/s, timeouts, retries, OOMs, and errors. Record peak/steady GPU memory in GiB with resident weights, KV cache, workspace, fragmentation, utilization, power, replica count, and native versus fallback kernel path. Compute cost from a declared accelerator/host/power or rental formula including failed work, and report paired deltas with confidence intervals.

Confounders and interpretation: stratify by prompt/output length, task, batch shape, concurrency, and kernel path. Control thermal/clock state, background load, cache state, autoscaling, placement, driver/runtime, admission limits, and run order. Audit that quantization calibration does not leak evaluation data and that unsupported operations do not silently dequantize. Do not attribute gains to a changed batch policy or relaxed SLO unless that is explicitly the deployment comparison.

Decision and rollback: keep only if all predeclared quality, correctness, safety, error, memory, and tail-latency gates pass and the minimum cost benefit is supported; otherwise reject for this workload or rewrite the plan. Canary behind a feature flag with capped traffic, retain the reference, and automatically roll back on gate breach or unexplained regression. Evidence remains provisional until manifests, traces, per-stratum results, confidence calculations, kernel audit, and cost assumptions are archived and reproducible.

kernel fallback, workspace, KV cache, or fragmentation can erase nominal memory savings
batching, thermal state, workload mix, and cost-model confounding
calibration/evaluation leakage or unsupported output behavior
evidence_required: checksummed artifacts and complete software/hardware manifest
held-out per-task quality and correctness results
repeated paired latency/throughput/memory trials with units and confidence intervals
kernel support/fallback and calibration-data audit
declared cost model plus canary and rollback telemetry

source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.

Scope and assumptions: freeze the model revision, tokenizer, prompt and output distributions, context-length strata, decoding settings, serving engine/version, hardware, runtime, quantization algorithm, bit-width, group size and scales, calibration split, batch/concurrency policy, and cost horizon. Compare the unquantized reference with the weight-only candidate using the same weights before quantization, prompts, seeds, stopping rules, request trace, SLOs, and replica policy; report measured facts with units and distinguish nominal weight storage from total runtime memory.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 210: at fixed quality and tail-latency gates, the quantized candidate lowers cost per accepted output token because reduced resident weight memory improves feasible packing or throughput without introducing material quality, correctness, kernel-support, or failure regressions. Falsify it if any required quality/correctness or p99/error/OOM gate fails, if the engine uses an unreported fallback path, or if a paired cost comparison does not exceed a prespecified minimum benefit. Treat effects as workload-stratum dependent rather than claiming a single average.

Experiment: freeze and checksum both artifacts and run a held-out quality/correctness suite covering each task, long and short contexts, rare tokens, structured outputs, safety/error cases, and representative decoding. Keep calibration data disjoint from evaluation. Use identical warmup, randomized run order, hardware pool, software manifest, and seeded request trace; repeat trials at prespecified offered loads and concurrency levels until uncertainty is adequate. Measure task-level quality, pass/malformed-output/refusal rates, TTFT and TPOT in milliseconds, p50/p95/p99 latency, queueing, requests/s and accepted output tokens/s, timeouts, retries, OOMs, and errors. Record peak/steady GPU memory in GiB with resident weights, KV cache, workspace, fragmentation, utilization, power, replica count, and native versus fallback kernel path. Compute cost from a declared accelerator/host/power or rental formula including failed work, and report paired deltas with confidence intervals.

Confounders and interpretation: stratify by prompt/output length, task, batch shape, concurrency, and kernel path. Control thermal/clock state, background load, cache state, autoscaling, placement, driver/runtime, admission limits, and run order. Audit that quantization calibration does not leak evaluation data and that unsupported operations do not silently dequantize.
